newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Dec corn drops to fresh 14-month low, harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Dec corn drops to fresh 14-month low, harvest.

text.p: Forecasts for good harvest weather in the U.S. Midwest now through next week pressed CBOT December corn to a fresh 14-month low by midsession, traders said.
"The good harvest weather all weekend is weighing on corn and the weakness in beans is weighing on corn," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
The session low for December as of 1135 CDT was $2.63-1/2 per bushel, the lowest level for that contract since $2.62-1/2 traded on August 30, 1995.
Traders said seasonal harvest pressure remains the key.
Meteorologists early Friday indicated cold but dry weather was expected in key harvesting areas over the weekend and warmer and dry weather was seen for next week.
"There should be a lot of harvesting," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.
Traders said corn continues to labor under the weight of a potential hike on November 12 by USDA in its estimate for 1996 U.S. corn production.
At 1140 CST, corn was two to three cents per bushel lower, with December down 2-3/4 at $2.63-1/4 a bushel.
Technicians said key technical indictors such as the closely-followed moving averages remain bearish.
But short term indicators showed the market was oversold.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December as of 1142 CST was at 13.5 points on a daily basis, 24 weekly and 38 points when computed monthly.
An RSI of 30 or less is generally considered indicative of an oversold market and 20 or less is viewed as very oversold.
